text: ‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 1› The prayer words spoken by Nabonidus, king of [Ba]bylon, [the] great king, [when he was afflicted …]
‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 2› … while in Teima, under the decree of G[o]d, he was struck by a grievous illness. I, Nabonidus, [was struck by illness …]
‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 3› I remained ill for seven years; then [God] turned [his] face toward me [and restored me …]
‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 4› … he released me from my guilt. The diviner was a Jew, [one] of the Judean exiles; he approached me and said …
‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 5› … “Tell this and put it in writing, to bring honor and renown to the name of [God Most High].” Thus I wrote …
‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 6› … “At Teima I endured a [grievous] illness, [by order of God Most High].”
‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 7› … “For seven years I kept praying [before] the gods of silver and gold, [copper and iron,]”
‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 8› … “wood, stone, and clay, since I had supposed that they were divine beings …”
‹4Q242 frg. 1–3, line 9› [The surviving line is too fragmentary for a reliable translation; most words are unreadable.]
‹4Q242 frg. 4, line 1› [Only scattered words remain: “… outside/beyond them … dreams …”. The sense and the damaged wording are uncertain; no continuous sentence can be restored securely.]
‹4Q242 frg. 4, line 2› [Scattered words may include “… from him … peace … my prosperity return to me …”; the reading is uncertain and does not yield a secure sentence.]
‹4Q242 frg. 4, line 3› [Scattered traces may read “… mercy … I could not …”; the damaged wording does not permit a secure sentence.]
‹4Q242 frg. 4, line 4› [Scattered traces may read “… how … are you …”; no continuous sentence can be restored securely.]
‹4Q242 frg. 4, line 5› [Fragmentary and unreadable; no continuous wording can be translated securely.]
